transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining me to review the esports team plan before I give final approval. As you know, the draft proposes registering a middle-school team for the spring interscholastic league with ten interested students, including Jordan, and practices from 3:30 to 5:00 on school days. Before I sign off, I'd like to hear your final operational checks. Coach, could you start by walking us through your review of the plan? And Counselor, I'd like your input as well. Please flag anything that needs adjustment -- logistics, facilities, student well-being, anything at all.

transcript.text: I need to flag several issues I found when I checked the league's current registration manual. A middle-school team may register exactly eight students — not ten as the draft plan currently lists. The team may field five active players per match. And critically, the league requires a wired local network rather than ordinary wireless, which means the draft plan's assumption about using the school's ordinary wireless network won't work. I have not yet entered these requirements in the activity proposal, so the plan as drafted does not reflect them.

transcript.text: Thank you, Mr. Nguyen, for those findings. Between the two of us, we've identified several items that need to be resolved before this plan is ready for approval. To summarize what needs adjustment: First, the roster must be reduced from ten to eight students per league rules. Second, the network requirement means we'll need a wired local network setup, not ordinary wireless. Third, Jordan's 4:15 p.m. practice constraint and the district van arrangement need to be incorporated into the plan. Ms. Brooks, I'd recommend we hold final approval until these issues are addressed in a revised plan. I'd also note that the 4:15 p.m. end time for Jordan may need to be considered alongside the practice schedule for all students, since the current 3:30 to 5:00 window doesn't accommodate it.

transcript.text: I agree with Ms. Carter's recommendation to hold final approval until we have a revised plan. To add to her summary on the logistics side: the roster reduction from ten to eight students will need a fair selection process, and since the league allows five active players per match, the coach staff will need to clarify how substitutes and playing time will work within the eight-student roster. On the network requirement, I'll need to work with our IT staff to determine whether we can set up a wired local network in our practice space, and that may have cost and setup-time implications we haven't accounted for yet. I'd also note that if practice needs to end by 4:15 p.m. to accommodate Jordan -- and potentially other students with similar constraints -- we should reconsider whether the 3:30 to 5:00 window is realistic at all, or whether we need a shorter practice schedule that works for the whole team. Once these items are addressed in a revised proposal, I'm ready to move forward.
